:::{#exm-entropy-chain-rule-noisy-copy}
#### Chain rule for entropy with a noisy copy
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

Let $X$ be a fair coin toss, coded $0$ or $1$.
Let $Y$ be a noisy copy of $X$:
it equals $X$ with [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $0.8$
and the other value with probability $0.2$.
The [joint distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-joint-distribution) gives probability $0.4$ to $(0, 0)$ and $(1, 1)$,
and $0.1$ to $(0, 1)$ and $(1, 0)$.
The chunk computes each [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) from its definition,
in [bits](#def-bit).

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
entropy <- function(p) -sum(p * log2(p))
joint <- matrix(
  data = c(0.4, 0.1, 0.1, 0.4),
  nrow = 2,
  dimnames = list(x = 0:1, y = 0:1)
)
p_y <- colSums(joint)
cond_x_given_y <- sweep(x = joint, MARGIN = 2, STATS = p_y, FUN = "/")
h_x_given_y_values <- apply(X = cond_x_given_y, MARGIN = 2, FUN = entropy)
h_x_given_y <- sum(p_y * h_x_given_y_values)
h_xy <- entropy(joint)
h_y <- entropy(p_y)
c(h_xy = h_xy, h_x_given_y = h_x_given_y, h_y = h_y)
```

The chunk computes $\entropyf{X \mid Y}$ as the average of the [entropies](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy) given each value of $Y$,
as in @thm-conditional-entropy-average with $X$ and $Y$ exchanged.
Here $\entropyf{X, Y} = `r round(h_xy, 3)`$ bits,
$\entropyf{X \mid Y} = `r round(h_x_given_y, 3)`$ bits
and $\entropyf{Y} = `r round(h_y, 3)`$ bits.
So $\entropyf{X \mid Y} + \entropyf{Y} = `r round(h_x_given_y + h_y, 3)`$ bits
agrees with $\entropyf{X, Y}$ (@cor-entropy-chain-rule-reversed),
and $\entropyf{X, Y} - \entropyf{Y} = `r round(h_xy - h_y, 3)`$ bits
agrees with $\entropyf{X \mid Y}$ (@cor-conditional-entropy-difference).

:::
